goldenPoints: Resting membrane potential of a neuron is about −70 mV; skeletal muscle about −90 mV
Smooth muscle has no troponin — calcium binds calmodulin and activates myosin light chain kinase
Resistance rises 81 times when vessel diameter falls to one-third (fourth-power law)
GFR is about 125 mL/min; creatinine clearance approximates it
Surfactant is made by type II pneumocytes and lowers alveolar surface tension
Carbon monoxide binds haemoglobin about 240 times more avidly than oxygen
Collecting duct reabsorbs the most water under ADH; thick ascending limb fluid is the most dilute
Growth hormone rises in stress, starvation and deep (NREM stage 3) sleep
Only Bombay (Oh) phenotype blood can be given to a Bombay phenotype patient
Hypophosphataemia — not hyperphosphataemia — is the hallmark electrolyte disturbance of refeeding syndrome
intro: Physiology carries 17 questions in every FMGE paper, and the brief shows a values-and-mechanisms paper: GFR numbers, curve shifts, reflex arcs, fibre types and hormone sources. Almost every stem is a standard Ganong fact wearing a clinical costume. Learn the numbers cold and the mechanisms once, properly.

subject: Physiology
tagline: FMGE Physiology is values and mechanisms — GFR, curve shifts, reflexes and fibre types, straight from Ganong.

topics.askedAs: Compartment volumes, Nernst values, LDH fraction
topics.oneLiner: 60–20–40: total body water 60%, ECF 20%, ICF 40% of body weight.
points: Total body water is about 60% of body weight in an adult man: intracellular fluid 40%, extracellular fluid 20% (plasma 5%, interstitial 15%)
Infants have a higher water fraction and relatively larger ECF — one reason dehydration hits infants harder and faster
Resting membrane potential: neuron about −70 mV, skeletal muscle about −90 mV; the Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase pumps 3 Na⁺ out for 2 K⁺ in
Equilibrium potential for K⁺ is about −90 mV and for Na⁺ about +60 mV (Nernst equation)
Lactate dehydrogenase is a cytosolic enzyme — on centrifugation it stays in the soluble (cytosolic) fraction, not in organelles
Lysosomal enzymes are stored in lysosomes, the cell's acidic digestive bags containing acid hydrolases
Cardiolipin is the signature phospholipid of the INNER mitochondrial membrane
DNA outside the nucleus exists in mitochondria — the basis of maternal inheritance of mitochondrial disorders
topics.title: Body Fluids, Membrane Potential & Cell Basics
topics.trap: Plasma is only about 5% of body weight (one-quarter of ECF) — stems love offering 20% (the whole ECF) as the plasma volume.

topics.oneLiner: Hypoxia B first, pressure A first, local anaesthetic C first.
points: Fibre types by speed: A-alpha fastest (up to 120 m/s) carrying proprioception and motor supply; C fibres slowest (about 1 m/s), carrying dull pain and temperature
Proprioception travels in large myelinated A-alpha (Ia/Ib) fibres
Fast, sharp, well-localised (superficial) pain travels in A-delta fibres; dull, aching pain in C fibres
Susceptibility to hypoxia: B fibres blocked first, then A, then C — preganglionic autonomic fibres fail earliest
Susceptibility to pressure: A fibres first, then B, then C — why a compressed arm loses touch and motor power before pain
Susceptibility to local anaesthetics: C fibres first, then B, then A — pain is blocked before touch
Conduction velocity rises with fibre diameter and with myelination (saltatory conduction between nodes of Ranvier)
Neuropraxia is a conduction block with the axon intact — segmental demyelination, complete recovery expected, the mildest nerve injury
topics.title: Nerve Fibres: Types, Speeds & Susceptibility
topics.trap: The three susceptibility orders are deliberately rotated in options — memorise the table, not a single sequence.

topics.askedAs: DHPR identity, malignant hyperthermia ion, calmodulin role
topics.oneLiner: Skeletal muscle: DHPR senses, RyR releases. Smooth muscle: calmodulin switches on MLCK.
points: In skeletal muscle the T-tubule voltage sensor is the dihydropyridine receptor (DHPR), which mechanically opens the ryanodine receptor (RyR1) on the sarcoplasmic reticulum
Malignant hyperthermia is a RyR1 defect: anaesthetic triggers cause uncontrolled Ca²⁺ release from the SR, rigidity and hyperthermia; treated with dantrolene
Calcium binds troponin C in skeletal and cardiac muscle, but in SMOOTH muscle it binds calmodulin, which activates myosin light chain kinase (MLCK)
Smooth muscle has no troponin and no sarcomeres; it can hold tension cheaply in the latch state
During exercise, contracting muscle increases local blood flow (metabolic vasodilation), raises venous return and switches on more motor units
Muscle spindle intrafusal fibres detect muscle LENGTH and its rate of change; Golgi tendon organs detect tension
Inhibiting the Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase (as digoxin does) raises intracellular Na⁺, slows Na⁺–Ca²⁺ exchange, raises intracellular Ca²⁺ and increases cardiac contractility
topics.title: Muscle Physiology: Skeletal, Cardiac & Smooth
topics.trap: 'Which is absent in smooth muscle?' — troponin. Calmodulin does its job there; sarcomeres and T-tubules are also lacking.

topics.askedAs: S1 timing, a/v wave meaning, PV loop phases
topics.oneLiner: S1 = systole begins; big a wave = stiff right heart inflow; giant v wave = tricuspid leak.
points: First heart sound (S1) is produced by closure of the mitral and tricuspid valves at the START of ventricular systole (isovolumetric contraction)
Second heart sound (S2) is closure of aortic and pulmonary valves at the start of diastole; it splits physiologically on inspiration
JVP a wave = atrial contraction; it is prominent in tricuspid stenosis and pulmonary hypertension, and giant 'cannon' a waves appear in complete heart block
JVP v wave = atrial filling against a closed tricuspid valve; a giant v wave signals tricuspid regurgitation
Pressure–volume loop: vertical segments are isovolumetric contraction (right side) and isovolumetric relaxation (left side); the top edge is ejection, the bottom edge is filling
Frank–Starling law: increased end-diastolic stretch increases force of contraction — the heart pumps what it receives
Stroke work and cardiac output rise with preload up to the plateau of the ventricular function curve
topics.title: Cardiac Cycle, Heart Sounds & JVP
topics.trap: The v wave is a filling wave, not a contraction wave — tricuspid regurgitation makes it giant, tricuspid stenosis makes the A wave prominent.

topics.oneLiner: Resistance follows the fourth power of radius — small narrowing, huge resistance.
points: Poiseuille law: resistance is inversely proportional to the fourth power of radius — reducing diameter to one-third raises resistance 3⁴ = 81 times
Total peripheral resistance is set mainly by arterioles, the resistance vessels; veins are the capacitance vessels holding most of the blood volume
Baroreceptor reflex: a rise in arterial pressure increases carotid sinus firing, increases vagal tone and cuts sympathetic outflow — heart rate and pressure fall back
Injected noradrenaline raises both systolic and diastolic pressure but heart rate FALLS — the baroreflex overrides its direct cardiac action
Mean arterial pressure = diastolic pressure + one-third of pulse pressure
Korotkoff sounds: first tapping sound marks systolic pressure; disappearance marks diastolic pressure in adults
Capillary filtration follows Starling forces: hydrostatic pressure pushes fluid out, plasma oncotic pressure (albumin) pulls it in
topics.title: Haemodynamics & Blood Pressure Control
topics.trap: Noradrenaline infusion causes reflex BRADYcardia despite being a cardiac stimulant — the baroreflex wins in the intact animal.

topics.askedAs: Surfactant cell, FEV1 pattern, volume identification
topics.oneLiner: Type II cells make surfactant; obstructive disease cuts FEV1/FVC, restrictive disease cuts volumes.
points: Surfactant is secreted by type II pneumocytes; it lowers alveolar surface tension and prevents end-expiratory collapse (atelectasis)
Normal volumes: tidal volume 500 mL, inspiratory reserve 3000 mL, expiratory reserve 1100 mL, residual volume 1200 mL; total lung capacity about 6000 mL
Residual volume cannot be measured by spirometry — it needs helium dilution or body plethysmography
FEV1/FVC ratio falls in obstructive disease (COPD, asthma); in restrictive disease both fall together and the ratio is normal or high
Ventilation–perfusion ratio averages about 0.8; it is highest at the lung apex and lowest at the base in the upright lung
Peripheral chemoreceptors (carotid bodies) sense falling PaO2 through oxygen-sensitive K⁺ channels — potassium efflux falls, the cell depolarises
Central chemoreceptors respond to CO2 via hydrogen ions in the cerebrospinal fluid — CO2 is the main driver of resting ventilation
topics.title: Respiratory Mechanics & Spirometry
topics.trap: Spirometry alone can never give residual volume or total lung capacity — any option deriving them from a spirometer tracing is wrong.

topics.askedAs: Curve shift factors, CO affinity, chloride shift name
topics.oneLiner: Right shift = tissues unloading: more CO2, more heat, more acid, more BPG.
points: Right shift of the oxygen–haemoglobin curve (easier unloading): increased CO2, increased temperature, increased 2,3-BPG, decreased pH (Bohr effect)
Left shift (tighter binding): the opposites, plus carbon monoxide, methaemoglobinaemia and fetal haemoglobin
P50 is about 27 mmHg — the PO2 at which haemoglobin is 50% saturated
Carbon monoxide binds haemoglobin about 240 times more avidly than oxygen and also shifts the curve left, starving tissues twice over
Chloride shift (Hamburger phenomenon): bicarbonate leaves the red cell in exchange for chloride entering, in systemic capillaries; it reverses in the lungs
Haldane effect: oxygenation of haemoglobin in the lungs drives CO2 off — the mirror image of the Bohr effect
Myoglobin has a hyperbolic curve and much higher affinity — it stores oxygen in muscle and releases it only at very low PO2
topics.title: Oxygen Transport & the Dissociation Curve
topics.trap: Stored blood loses 2,3-BPG, so transfused blood holds oxygen tighter (left shift) — a stem about stored blood expects this.

topics.askedAs: GFR value, ADH site, renin source
topics.oneLiner: GFR 125; PCT does the bulk; collecting duct answers ADH; JG cells release renin.
points: Normal GFR is about 125 mL/min (180 L/day); creatinine clearance approximates GFR and is the bedside estimate used in practice
Proximal convoluted tubule reabsorbs about 65% of filtrate — all the glucose and amino acids, most Na⁺, water and bicarbonate
The diluting segment (thick ascending limb) produces the most dilute tubular fluid — it reabsorbs NaCl without water via NKCC2, the loop diuretic target
Under ADH, the collecting duct reabsorbs the most water — aquaporin-2 channels are inserted into principal cells
Renin is secreted by juxtaglomerular (granular) cells of the afferent arteriole; the macula densa senses NaCl delivery
Haemoglobin is not filtered because of its size and the negative charge barrier of the glomerular basement membrane
Filtration fraction is about 20% of renal plasma flow; afferent constriction lowers GFR, efferent constriction (angiotensin II) initially preserves it
Substances like PAH are secreted and nearly completely cleared — PAH clearance estimates renal plasma flow
topics.title: Renal Physiology & GFR
topics.trap: 'Segment with lowest osmolality under ADH' is the thick ascending limb outlet (diluting segment) — not the collecting duct, which concentrates under ADH.

topics.askedAs: Enteropeptidase site, iron absorption enhancer, second messenger
topics.oneLiner: Enteropeptidase lights the pancreatic cascade; vitamin C rescues iron; histamine works through cAMP.
points: Enteropeptidase (enterokinase) is produced by the duodenal brush border and activates trypsinogen to trypsin, which then activates all other pancreatic proteases
Motilin drives the migrating motor complex — the housekeeping peristaltic waves of the fasting gut; peristalsis itself is coordinated by the myenteric (Auerbach) plexus
Histamine stimulates gastric acid via H2 receptors using cAMP as second messenger; gastrin and acetylcholine act through Ca²⁺
Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) enhances dietary iron absorption by reducing ferric to absorbable ferrous iron; tea and phytates inhibit it
Secretin (from S cells) drives bicarbonate-rich pancreatic juice in response to acid; CCK drives enzyme-rich secretion and gallbladder contraction in response to fat
Bile salts are reabsorbed in the terminal ileum (enterohepatic circulation) — ileal disease causes fat malabsorption and gallstones
The vomiting centre lies in the medulla; the chemoreceptor trigger zone is the area postrema, outside the blood–brain barrier
topics.title: GI Physiology: Motility, Secretions & Absorption
topics.trap: Enteropeptidase is a BRUSH BORDER enzyme of the duodenum, not a pancreatic secretion — the pancreas ships zymogens, the gut activates them.

topics.oneLiner: GH loves stress, starvation and deep sleep; TBG carries thyroxine; prolactin grows the breast.
points: Growth hormone secretion increases during stress, starvation (hypoglycaemia) and deep sleep (NREM stage 3) — GH is a fasting, anabolic-to-protein hormone
Thyroxine-binding globulin (TBG) is the principal carrier of thyroxine in plasma; most circulating T4 is protein-bound, only free T4 is active
Prolactin is responsible for mammary gland growth and milk production; oxytocin causes milk ejection (let-down)
Insulin is the fed-state hormone: it promotes glycogenesis, lipogenesis and protein synthesis and suppresses gluconeogenesis and lipolysis
Glucagon acts mainly on the liver to raise glucose — glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis; it has no significant action on muscle glycogen
Cortisol is permissive for catecholamine action, maintains vascular tone, and is anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive at high levels
Aldosterone acts on the collecting duct to retain Na⁺ and water and excrete K⁺ and H⁺; it is driven by angiotensin II and hyperkalaemia
Parathyroid hormone raises plasma Ca²⁺ (bone resorption, renal Ca reabsorption, calcitriol activation); calcitonin plays a minor opposing role in adults
topics.title: Endocrine Physiology: Pituitary, Thyroid & Adrenal
topics.trap: Prolactin makes milk, oxytocin ejects it — stems routinely swap the two in lactation questions.

topics.askedAs: Sertoli vs Leydig products, inhibin target
topics.oneLiner: Sertoli nurses sperm and makes inhibin B; Leydig makes testosterone.
points: Sertoli cells secrete inhibin B, which selectively suppresses FSH secretion from the anterior pituitary
Leydig (interstitial) cells secrete testosterone under LH control; Sertoli cells work under FSH and testosterone
Sertoli cells also make androgen-binding protein and form the blood–testis barrier
The LH surge triggers ovulation about 36 hours later and converts the ruptured follicle into the corpus luteum
Oestrogen feedback is negative most of the cycle but switches to positive feedback at mid-cycle to generate the LH surge
Spermatogenesis takes about 74 days; sperm mature and gain motility in the epididymis
hCG from the syncytiotrophoblast rescues the corpus luteum in early pregnancy — the basis of the urine pregnancy test
topics.title: Reproductive Physiology
topics.trap: Inhibin suppresses FSH only, not LH — and in males it comes from Sertoli cells, in females from granulosa cells.

topics.askedAs: Bombay transfusion, Ig ranking, ABG derived value
topics.oneLiner: Bombay takes only Bombay; IgG is the most abundant; bicarbonate is calculated, not measured.
points: Immunoglobulin G is the most abundant immunoglobulin in serum and the only one crossing the placenta; IgA dominates secretions; IgM is the largest and first produced
A patient with Bombay (Oh) phenotype has anti-H antibodies and can receive ONLY Bombay phenotype blood — even group O blood will haemolyse
On an ABG report, pH, PaO2 and PaCO2 are measured; bicarbonate (and base excess) are CALCULATED from them using Henderson–Hasselbalch
High altitude causes hypoxic hypoxia: hyperventilation, respiratory alkalosis, then acclimatisation with raised 2,3-BPG and polycythaemia
The Bezold–Jarisch reflex — bradycardia, hypotension and apnoea from stimulating ventricular chemoreceptors (e.g. by contrast or irritant chemicals)
Refeeding syndrome: refeeding a starved patient spikes insulin and drives phosphate, potassium and magnesium INTO cells — hypophosphataemia is the hallmark
Body temperature is regulated by the anterior hypothalamus (preoptic area); fever is a raised set-point driven by prostaglandin E2
Albumin is the main determinant of plasma oncotic pressure — low albumin (nephrotic syndrome, liver failure) causes oedema
topics.title: Blood, Immunity, ABG & Special States
topics.trap: Bombay phenotype blood looks like group O on forward grouping but the patient will react to O blood — reverse grouping and anti-H testing expose it.
